questions.q: Which one of the following is a Kharif crop of India?
questions.e: Cotton is sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon (May-July) and picked in autumn. Mustard, gram and barley are sown in October-December and harvested in spring, so they are Rabi crops.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain
questions.h: Cotton: sown with the rains, picked in autumn

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Zaid crops are grown in the short season between Rabi harvest and Kharif sowing, mostly with irrigation.
2. Rice is grown only in the Kharif season in every Indian state.
3. Wheat is a Rabi crop that needs a cool growing season and warm weather at ripening.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Zaid (March-June) crops such as watermelon and cucumber need irrigation, and wheat is a cool-season Rabi crop. Statement 2 is wrong: Boro rice in West Bengal and Assam and winter rice in Tamil Nadu and Andhra are grown outside Kharif.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about price policy for agricultural produce:
1. Minimum Support Prices are announced by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
2. The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
3. For sugarcane, the price announced by the Centre is called the Fair and Remunerative Price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CACP is an attached office of the Agriculture Ministry, not a statutory body, so statement 2 fails. CCEA approves MSP on its advice, and sugarcane has a separate FRP under the Sugarcane (Control) Order.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Agriculture); PIB

questions.q:
With reference to Minimum Support Price (MSP) in India, consider the following statements:
1. MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops, while sugarcane has a separate Fair and Remunerative Price.
2. The National Food Security Act, 2013 gives farmers a legal right to MSP.
3. Potato and tomato are among the crops for which MSP is announced.
4. The Cotton Corporation of India acts as a nodal agency for price support operations in cotton.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 22 mandated crops cover cereals, pulses, oilseeds and commercial crops such as cotton and jute, and CCI does price support for cotton. The NFSA deals with subsidised foodgrain entitlements, not a legal MSP right, and perishable vegetables like potato and tomato have no MSP.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy; PIB

questions.q: The Planning Commission, for the purpose of regional agricultural planning, divided India into how many agro-climatic regions?
questions.e: The Planning Commission demarcated 15 broad agro-climatic regions, based on soil, climate and cropping patterns. The figure 127 belongs to the more detailed agro-climatic zones of the ICAR National Agricultural Research Project.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest source of irrigation in India in terms of net irrigated area?
questions.e: Groundwater based wells and tube wells irrigate more than half of India's net irrigated area, helped by electricity subsidies and the Green Revolution. Canals are second, and tanks are important mainly in peninsular India.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Economic Survey
questions.h: Wells beat canals: groundwater irrigates most land

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jute - West Bengal
2. Saffron - Himachal Pradesh
3. Rubber - Kerala
4. Tea - Karnataka
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched in terms of the leading producing state?
questions.e: West Bengal is the leading jute state and Kerala dominates natural rubber. Saffron is grown at Pampore and in Kishtwar in Jammu and Kashmir, and Assam, not Karnataka, leads in tea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about black (regur) soil:
1. It is formed from the weathering of Deccan Trap basalt.
2. It retains moisture for long and develops deep cracks in the dry season.
3. It is rich in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Basalt parent rock gives clayey soil that swells when wet and cracks when dry, which suits cotton. The soil is rich in lime, iron, magnesium and potash but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Geography Ch 6; Majid Husain
questions.h: Regur: lime, iron, magnesium, potash rich; N, P, humus poor (cotton soil)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Laterite soils are generally poor in fertility and need heavy manuring for most crops.
Statement-II: Intense leaching under heavy rainfall removes silica and nutrients, leaving behind iron and aluminium oxides.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: In hot, wet climates with alternating wet and dry spells, water washes soluble bases and silica downward, which impoverishes the topsoil. That leaching is exactly why laterite supports only tea, coffee, cashew and similar crops with manuring.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Geography Ch 6
questions.h: Heavy rain washes nutrients out, leaving rusty iron

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Soil Health Card Scheme:
1. It was launched in 2015 from Suratgarh in Rajasthan.
2. The card reports the status of 12 parameters including nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH and organic carbon.
3. A fresh card is issued to every farmer every five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The card gives crop-wise nutrient recommendations so farmers can balance fertiliser use. The cycle is two years, not five, because soil nutrient status changes with cropping and fertiliser use.
questions.s: PIB; Economic Survey

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PM-KISAN:
1. It provides income support of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments.
2. States bear 40 percent of the cost of the scheme.
3. It was initially meant for small and marginal farmer families but was later extended to all landholding farmer families.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-KISAN started in 2019 and the coverage was widened later that year to remove the landholding ceiling. It is a Central Sector Scheme funded fully by the Centre, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Green Revolution in India:
1. It was initially concentrated on wheat in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
2. It reduced inter-regional disparities in agricultural productivity.
3. It depended on high-yielding varieties of seeds, chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The package of HYV seeds, fertiliser and irrigation worked best in areas with assured water, so it first helped north-west India. Because other regions and rainfed crops lagged, it widened regional disparities rather than narrowing them.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India Since Independence; Ramesh Singh
questions.h: Seeds + fertiliser + water = Green Revolution, but only where water was assured

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agriculture and greenhouse gases:
1. Flooded paddy fields emit methane.
2. Enteric fermentation in ruminant livestock emits methane.
3. Application of nitrogenous fertilisers is the main source of agricultural methane.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Anaerobic decomposition in waterlogged soils and microbes in the rumen both produce methane. Nitrogen fertilisers chiefly lead to nitrous oxide emissions, so statement 3 confuses the gas.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Economic Survey

questions.q: Which one of the following is a feature of the System of Rice Intensification (SRI)?
o: Continuous flooding of the field throughout the crop cycle
Transplanting of young seedlings with wide spacing and alternate wetting and drying instead of continuous flooding
Dense planting of several old seedlings per hill
Broadcasting of seed directly into standing water
questions.e: SRI saves water and seed by using young single seedlings, wide spacing and intermittent irrigation, which also reduces methane from paddy. Continuous flooding and dense, older seedlings are features of conventional practice.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; Economic Survey

questions.q: The enrichment of water bodies with nitrates and phosphates from fertiliser run-off, causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion, is known as
questions.e: Excess nutrients feed algae, and when the algae die their decomposition consumes dissolved oxygen, harming fish. Biomagnification refers to increasing toxin concentration along a food chain.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; NCERT Class XII Biology
questions.h: Fertiliser runoff -> algae -> oxygen crash = eutrophication

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state.
2. The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana is a component of the Soil Health Management scheme under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture.
3. The Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region is meant for Sikkim only.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sikkim achieved fully organic status in 2016, and PKVY promotes cluster based organic farming. The north-eastern value chain mission covers all eight north-eastern states, not just Sikkim.
questions.s: PIB; Economic Survey

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of dam and river:
1. Hirakud - Mahanadi
2. Nagarjuna Sagar - Krishna
3. Mettur - Cauvery
4. Jayakwadi - Narmada
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Hirakud is in Odisha on the Mahanadi, Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, and Mettur on the Cauvery in Tamil Nadu. Jayakwadi in Maharashtra is on the Godavari.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, the 'Per Drop More Crop' component primarily promotes
o: Procurement of foodgrains at support prices
Micro irrigation such as drip and sprinkler systems
questions.e: The component raises water use efficiency by subsidising drip and sprinkler irrigation, so more crop is grown per unit of water. Insurance, soil testing and procurement sit under other schemes.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, the maximum premium payable by farmers for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops is
questions.e: The farmer pays 2 percent for Kharif foodgrain and oilseeds, 1.5 percent for Rabi, and 5 percent for annual commercial and horticultural crops. The rest of the premium is shared by the Centre and states.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Statement-I: Including legumes in a crop rotation improves soil fertility.
Statement-II: Root nodules of leguminous plants host Rhizobium bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Rhizobium in nodules converts atmospheric nitrogen into forms the plant can use, and the leftover nitrogen benefits the next crop. That is why pulses are rotated with cereals.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: Which one of the following is used for the reclamation of alkaline (sodic) soils such as reh and usar?
questions.e: Gypsum supplies calcium that replaces exchangeable sodium on soil particles, which is then leached out with drained water. Lime is used for acidic soils.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India; Shankar IAS
questions.h: Alkaline soil needs gypsum; acidic soil needs lime

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about neem coated urea:
1. All urea produced domestically or imported for agriculture is required to be neem coated.
2. Neem coating accelerates nitrification and so releases nitrogen to the plant faster.
3. It helps reduce diversion of subsidised urea to non-agricultural uses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Neem coating makes the urea unsuitable for industrial use and so curbs diversion. It slows nitrification, not accelerates it, so the nitrogen is released slowly and losses fall.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh
questions.h: Neem slows nitrification, so urea stays in soil longer

questions.q:
Statement-I: Urea is used in much larger quantities in India than phosphatic and potassic fertilisers relative to the recommended ratio.
Statement-II: Urea is outside the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme and is sold at a government-fixed maximum retail price.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Nutrient Based Subsidy since 2010 covers only phosphatic and potassic fertilisers, whose prices float. The relatively cheap controlled price of urea pushes farmers to overuse nitrogen and skews the N:P:K ratio.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy; Economic Survey

questions.q: 'Retting', a process of soaking the stems in water to separate the fibres, is associated with which crop?
questions.e: Jute stems are bundled and kept in slow flowing or stagnant water, where microbes loosen the fibre. This is why jute is concentrated in the humid, water-rich Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of 'Revolution' and the product associated with it:
1. White Revolution - Milk
2. Yellow Revolution - Oilseeds
3. Blue Revolution - Fish
4. Green Revolution - Foodgrains
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Operation Flood under the NDDB boosted milk, the Yellow Revolution boosted oilseeds, the Blue Revolution fisheries and the Green Revolution wheat and rice. All the pairs are therefore correct.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sugarcane in India:
1. India is the second largest producer of sugarcane in the world after Brazil.
2. Sugarcane is a Rabi crop sown in October and harvested in April.
3. Yields per hectare are generally higher in peninsular India than in the northern plains because of the longer growing season and absence of winter frost.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sugarcane is a tropical crop that needs a hot, humid climate and a long growing season, so the frost-free peninsula gives higher yields. It is an annual crop that stays in the field for 10 to 18 months, so it is not a Rabi crop.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about millets:
1. The United Nations declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets on a proposal moved by India.
2. Jowar, bajra and ragi are important millets grown in India.
3. Millets need heavy irrigation and fertile alluvial soil.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Millets are hardy, drought-tolerant coarse grains that thrive on poor soils and low rainfall, which is why they are called climate-resilient crops. Statement 3 describes the opposite of their growing needs.
questions.s: PIB; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: Which one of the following pulses accounts for the largest share of India's total pulse production?
questions.e: Gram is the main Rabi pulse and contributes the largest share of production, with Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan as important producing states. Tur, moong and urad together make up a smaller share.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Economic Survey

questions.q: Which one of the following states is the largest producer of soybean in India?
questions.e: Madhya Pradesh grows the largest share of the soybean crop on its black soils and is sometimes called the soya state, with Maharashtra as the second state. Soybean is a Kharif oilseed.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of cotton cultivation in India?
o: It requires at least 210 frost-free days
It is a Rabi crop grown in winter under frost conditions
It grows well in the black soils of the Deccan plateau
It is sown in spring or early summer and picked in autumn
questions.e: Cotton is a tropical to sub-tropical Kharif crop that cannot tolerate frost and needs a long, warm growing season. The black soils hold moisture well for the crop.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: Which one of the following regions is the largest tea producing region of India?
questions.e: Assam produces more than half of India's tea, mostly in the Brahmaputra valley with its warm, humid climate and well drained acid soils. Darjeeling, Nilgiri and Kangra are smaller but well known producers.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: Tank irrigation is common in the peninsular plateau of India.
Statement-II: Undulating terrain and impervious hard rocks of the plateau make it easy to build tanks and difficult to recharge groundwater for wells.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Rain water is collected in natural depressions and bunded tanks in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. In the northern alluvial plains, soft permeable soil makes wells and canals more suitable.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: In a region, the net sown area is 200 hectares and the gross cropped area is 300 hectares. What is the cropping intensity?
questions.e: Cropping intensity is gross cropped area divided by net sown area, multiplied by 100, so 300 divided by 200 gives 150 percent. It shows that on average land is cropped one and a half times a year.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about alluvial soils of the Ganga plains:
1. Khadar is the newer alluvium of floodplains and is more fertile.
2. Bhangar is the older alluvium and contains kankar (calcareous) nodules.
3. Bhangar lies in the low flood-prone areas and is renewed by floods every year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Khadar is renewed by annual floods and is therefore fertile, while Bhangar lies on higher terraces above the flood level. Statement 3 swaps the position of the two types.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Geography Ch 6

questions.q: The badland topography of the Chambal ravines is mainly the result of which type of soil erosion?
questions.e: Running water cuts deep channels into soft alluvium and widens them into gullies, which make the land unfit for cultivation. Sheet erosion removes a thin uniform layer over a wide area.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Geography Ch 6; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of shifting cultivation and region:
1. Jhum - North-eastern India
2. Podu - Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
3. Bewar - Rajasthan
4. Milpa - Central America and Mexico
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Jhum is the north-east name, Podu is used in Andhra and Odisha, and Milpa is the Central American name. Bewar is the name used in Madhya Pradesh, not Rajasthan.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5; Majid Husain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about crop residue burning in north-west India:
1. The short gap between paddy harvest and wheat sowing encourages farmers to burn stubble.
2. The smoke contributes to winter air pollution in Delhi and surrounding regions.
3. The Pusa Decomposer is a chemical fertiliser that is applied to the soil to replace stubble burning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Because the field must be cleared quickly for wheat, burning is the cheapest option, and winter calm air traps the smoke. The Pusa Decomposer is a microbial capsule solution that speeds up decomposition of the straw, not a chemical fertiliser.
questions.s: PIB; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: The health disaster linked to aerial spraying of the pesticide endosulfan on cashew plantations was reported from which district?
questions.e: Years of aerial spraying on cashew estates in Kasaragod were linked to birth defects and illness among local people. Endosulfan was later banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q: In India, the approval for the environmental release of genetically modified crops is given by the
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
questions.e: GEAC functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and appraises GM organisms for environmental release under the Environment (Protection) Act rules. Bt cotton was approved on its recommendation in 2002.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the e-NAM (National Agriculture Market):
1. It was launched in 2016 as a pan-India electronic trading portal.
2. The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium is the lead implementing agency.
3. It abolishes the Agricultural Produce Market Committee mandis and replaces them with private markets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: e-NAM integrates existing APMC mandis into one online platform so farmers can reach buyers across states. It does not abolish the mandis.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: The Food Corporation of India was established in 1965 under which one of the following Acts?
questions.e: The Food Corporations Act of 1964 created FCI after the food shortages of the early 1960s, to procure grain at support prices and hold buffer stocks. The Essential Commodities Act regulates trade and stock limits.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of ICAR institute and location:
1. Central Rice Research Institute - Cuttack
2. Central Potato Research Institute - Shimla
3. Sugarcane Breeding Institute - Coimbatore
4. Central Tuber Crops Research Institute - Chennai
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The rice institute is at Cuttack in Odisha, the potato institute at Shimla and the sugarcane institute at Coimbatore. The tuber crops institute is at Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Statement-I: Winter rainfall from western disturbances is beneficial to Rabi wheat in north-west India.
Statement-II: Western disturbances are mid-latitude systems from the Mediterranean region that bring light winter rain to the north-west.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: These disturbances come with the westerly jet stream and give the north-west light rain in December to February. This moisture is needed for the cool-season wheat crop at a time when the monsoon is absent.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Geography Ch 4

questions.q: Growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in definite row patterns is known as
questions.e: In intercropping, the crops are arranged in distinct rows, for example soybean with pigeon pea. In mixed cropping seeds are mixed without a definite pattern, and rotation is growing crops one after another in sequence.
questions.s: Shankar IAS; NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT used as a biofertiliser?
questions.e: Bacillus thuringiensis produces the Bt toxin and is used as a biopesticide against insects. Azolla with its symbiotic cyanobacteria, free-living Nostoc and Rhizobium all fix atmospheric nitrogen.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Shankar IAS

questions.q: Operation Greens, launched in 2018, primarily aims to stabilise the supply and prices of which crops?
questions.e: It is a scheme of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries to reduce price volatility of perishable vegetables through processing and storage. Pulses, cereals and commercial crops are covered by other mechanisms.
questions.s: PIB; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scheme for formation and promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations:
1. It was launched in 2020 as a Central Sector Scheme.
2. NABARD, NCDC and SFAC are among its implementing agencies.
3. Farmer Producer Organisations can be registered only under cooperative society laws.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme helps small farmers gain bargaining power through collective marketing and bulk input purchase. FPOs may also be registered as producer companies under the Companies Act, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: PIB; Economic Survey

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order of launch, from earliest to latest:
A. High Yielding Varieties Programme
B. Operation Flood
C. Soil Health Card Scheme
D. PM-KISAN
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The seed-fertiliser programme began in 1966-67, followed by Operation Flood in 1970 for dairy. Soil Health Card came in 2015 and PM-KISAN in 2019.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India Since Independence; PIB
questions.h: Seeds, then milk, then soil, then cash

questions.q:
Statement-I: Wheat cultivation in India is concentrated in the northern plains.
Statement-II: Wheat requires a hot and humid climate with very heavy rainfall during the growing season.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Wheat is a Rabi crop that needs a cool growing season, bright sunshine at ripening and moderate rainfall of about 50 to 75 cm, which suits the Indo-Gangetic plain. Heavy rainfall and humidity encourage rust and damage the crop.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PM-KUSUM:
1. It is implemented by the Ministry of Power.
2. It supports farmers in installing standalone solar-powered agricultural pumps.
3. It supports the solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme is run by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and aims to cut diesel use and power subsidy in irrigation. It also lets farmers sell surplus solar power to the grid.
questions.s: PIB; Economic Survey
